mathematicalReview.reason: For each main index use its sole leaf when present,otherwise the main station. A pair attached to different main indices is bounded by these representatives. A same-index main/leaf distance d_i is bounded by representative i to any other representative because N>=2. Hence only distinct-index pairs determine the diameter;2d_i must not be introduced.

mathematicalReview.obligation: shortcut orientation and ignoring good old pairs
mathematicalReview.reason: A simple positive-weight shortest path uses the new edge at most once;the direct path and two endpoint orientations exhaust possible walks after removing loops. For ordered original indices and ordered endpoints,the uncrossed orientation is no longer. Thus a pair with olddistance<=K imposes no condition,whereas every olddistance>K pair must satisfy di+dj+c+|xi-y|+|xj-z|<=K.

Apply |p|+|q|=max(|p+q|,|p-q|) to p=y-xi,q=z-xj. S=y+z lies in[bi+bj+c-K,ai+aj+K-c];D=z-y lies in[bj-ai+c-K,aj-bi+K-c]. Negative residual budget makes these bounds inconsistent. Non-strict closed bounds are correct for distance<=K;oldpair selection alone uses strict>K.

mathematicalReview.obligation: top-two branch lower bound and eligible orientation
mathematicalReview.reason: Every representative distance is at least di+dj. The two largest branch values from distinct indices,including multiplicity for ties,give a necessary lower bound. Above it,an eligible a_i<b_j-K with i>j is impossible because b_j-a_i=di+dj-(xi-xj)<di+dj<=K. Only i<j orself remains;self may qualify when2d_j>K and is explicitly excluded.

Sort two index-bearing station arrays once by a andb. As j runs in increasingb,the strict a-threshold only increases;each index is inserted once. Store two minima ofa and two maxima ofb with distinct indices;equal values are retained while slots are populated. Excluding j picks the first retained candidate unless it isj,then the second. Four extrema can be realized by different pairs because bounds are intersected independently.

mathematicalReview.obligation: station-only endpoints and complete V-shaped pointer
mathematicalReview.reason: For y=x_u,the feasible z interval is[max(Slo-y,y+Dlo),min(Shi-y,y+Dhi)]. Choosing the first original station at orabove the lower bound with index>=u+1 is necessary and sufficient. The lower bound is the max of one decreasing andone increasing line;its lower_bound index is nonincreasing then nondecreasing. Taking max with increasingu+1 can only replace a terminal part of the decreasing phase,hence preserves a single valley. Starting the pointer atN and moving both directions gives atmostN left andN right moves. SentinelN,exact equality,inverted boxes andforbidden equal indices are correctly handled.

Adding a positive edge never increases a distance;original station diameter is a feasible upper bound for any legal distinct pair. Feasibility is monotone. The original diameter is atmost1000001000000000<2^50,so atmost50binary decisions suffice. Negative K is rejected;K>=original returns before rotated arithmetic. All remaining production boundary/pointer intermediates are less than1e16 in magnitude.

Adding delta to every branch increases each distinct-index representative distance by exactly2delta for every fixed shortcut endpoint pair. The representative lemma holds before andafter,even when a zero branch becomes a real leaf. Consequently both the optimum and every fixed-endpoint diameter increase by2delta. New literal BFS instances independently confirm the effect without using representative reduction in their oracle.
